title: A Veto From the Null Side

scenes.tts: A cell in a rabbit's eye fires hard for a spot moving right. Moving left, it barely fires. How does it know?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Veto From the Null Side. A ganglion cell with a spike raster: a spot moving right gives a dense raster, the same spot moving left a sparse one. Question on screen: how does it know?
scenes.narration: A cell in a rabbit's eye fires hard for a spot moving right. Moving left, it barely fires. How does it know?

scenes.tts: The direction that drives it is its preferred direction. The opposite way is its null direction.
scenes.visual: Labels appear beside the two rasters: preferred direction (dense), null direction (sparse).
scenes.narration: The direction that drives it is its preferred direction. The opposite way is its null direction.

scenes.tts: Barlow and Hill reported such cells in rabbit retina in nineteen sixty-three.
scenes.caption: Barlow and Hill reported such cells in rabbit retina in 1963.
scenes.visual: Label: Barlow and Hill, 1963, rabbit retina.
scenes.narration: Barlow and Hill reported such cells in rabbit retina in 1963.

scenes.tts: Two years later, Barlow and Levick asked how it works.
scenes.visual: Label: Barlow and Levick, 1965, how does it work?
scenes.narration: Two years later, Barlow and Levick asked how it works.

scenes.tts: They flashed two neighbouring spots in the cell's field, spot ay and spot bee, one after the other.
scenes.caption: They flashed two neighbouring spots in the cell's field, spot A and spot B, one after the other.
scenes.visual: A receptive field outline with two small spots side by side, labelled A (left) and B (right). Preferred arrow points right.
scenes.narration: They flashed two neighbouring spots in the cell's field, spot A and spot B, one after the other.

scenes.tts: Ay then bee is a small jump in the preferred direction. Bee then ay is a jump in the null direction.
scenes.caption: A then B is a small jump in the preferred direction. B then A is a jump in the null direction.
scenes.visual: Arrows: A then B, rightward, labelled preferred order; B then A, leftward, labelled null order.
scenes.narration: A then B is a small jump in the preferred direction. B then A is a jump in the null direction.

scenes.tts: If the two flashes simply added, the pair would reach the dashed line in either order.
scenes.visual: Bar chart with illustrative numbers: A alone 4 spikes, B alone 4 spikes, dashed line at 8 marked: simple sum. Small note: illustrative, not Barlow and Levick's data.
scenes.narration: If the two flashes simply added, the pair would reach the dashed line in either order.

scenes.tts: Predict. Under a veto, which order falls below the line? Under a boost, which order rises above it?
scenes.visual: Two empty bars beside the dashed line at 8, labelled A then B and B then A. On screen: which order falls below 8? which rises above?
scenes.narration: Predict. Under a veto, which order falls below the line? Under a boost, which order rises above it?

scenes.tts: A veto leaves a deficit in the null order. A boost leaves a surplus in the preferred order.
scenes.visual: The B then A bar fills to 2, remainder shown as minus 6 under a veto label; the A then B bar fills to 14, remainder plus 6 under a boost label. On screen: remainder = paired minus sum.
scenes.narration: A veto leaves a deficit in the null order. A boost leaves a surplus in the preferred order.

scenes.tts: Barlow and Levick found a big deficit in the null order. The preferred order gave about the sum.
scenes.visual: The boost bar fades back to about the dashed line; the null-order bar stays low, with the count and remainder labels removed. Label: the pattern Barlow and Levick found; bar heights illustrative.
scenes.narration: Barlow and Levick found a big deficit in the null order. The preferred order gave about the sum.

scenes.tts: So the main operation in this cell is a veto.
scenes.visual: Word on screen: veto.
scenes.narration: So the main operation in this cell is a veto.

scenes.tts: They also inferred that the veto is local, working in small subunits across the field.
scenes.visual: The receptive field divides into a grid of small patches, each with its own tiny veto symbol.
scenes.narration: They also inferred that the veto is local, working in small subunits across the field.

scenes.tts: Here is a simple sketch. To cancel excitation, inhibition must overlap it in time.
scenes.visual: Two traces on one time axis: an excitation bump and an inhibition bump. Where they overlap, spikes are cancelled; inhibition that lags leaves the early spikes. Label: simple circuit sketch.
scenes.narration: Here is a simple sketch. To cancel excitation, inhibition must overlap it in time.

scenes.tts: Null motion should start the inhibition early, so it should come from where null motion starts. Call that the null side.
scenes.visual: A spot moves left across the ganglion cell. The right-hand side, where it starts, is shaded and labelled null side. The inhibition trace overlaps the excitation trace. Label: circuit sketch.
scenes.narration: Null motion should start the inhibition early, so it should come from where null motion starts. Call that the null side.

scenes.tts: Preferred motion reaches the excitation first. The inhibition lags behind, so the excitation gets a head start.
scenes.visual: A spot moves right. The excitation trace starts first; the inhibition trace starts later. Label: excitation leads.
scenes.narration: Preferred motion reaches the excitation first. The inhibition lags behind, so the excitation gets a head start.

scenes.tts: Barlow and Levick were tentative about which cells supply it. Most of it turned out to come from starburst amacrine cells.
scenes.visual: A question mark over the null side resolves into a starburst amacrine cell growing in.
scenes.narration: Barlow and Levick were tentative about which cells supply it. Most of it turned out to come from starburst amacrine cells.

scenes.tts: Its dendrites radiate like the spokes of a wheel.
scenes.visual: Plan view of a starburst cell: a soma with four spokes radiating out.
scenes.narration: Its dendrites radiate like the spokes of a wheel.

scenes.tts: Each dendrite is its own small direction detector. It is most active when motion runs outward, from cell body to tip.
scenes.visual: One spoke lights brightly for a spot moving outward along it, and stays dim for a spot moving inward. Label: outward = most active.
scenes.narration: Each dendrite is its own small direction detector. It is most active when motion runs outward, from cell body to tip.

scenes.tts: Take a ganglion cell that prefers rightward motion. It is wired mainly to starburst branches that point left, its null direction.
scenes.visual: A gold ganglion cell is placed over the starburst cells. Mostly left-pointing spokes make prominent contacts, marked with gold synapse dots; a few other spokes make small, faint contacts. Most starburst somata sit to the right, on the null side. Label: illustrative sketch.
scenes.narration: Take a ganglion cell that prefers rightward motion. It is wired mainly to starburst branches that point left, its null direction.

scenes.tts: Leftward motion runs outward along those branches. Their inhibition is strongest, and the ganglion cell stays quiet.
scenes.visual: A spot sweeps left: the connected spokes light as the spot sweeps toward the ganglion cell's inputs; its raster stays sparse.
scenes.narration: Leftward motion runs outward along those branches. Their inhibition is strongest, and the ganglion cell stays quiet.

scenes.tts: Rightward motion runs inward along the same branches. They release little, so the excitation wins.
scenes.visual: A spot sweeps right: the connected spokes stay dim; the ganglion cell's raster is dense.
scenes.narration: Rightward motion runs inward along the same branches. They release little, so the excitation wins.

scenes.tts: So remember the sign. The strongest inhibition comes from dendrites that prefer roughly the direction the ganglion cell ignores.
scenes.visual: On-screen rule over the animation: the strongest inhibition comes from dendrites that prefer roughly the direction the DSGC ignores.
scenes.narration: So remember the sign. The strongest inhibition comes from dendrites that prefer roughly the direction the ganglion cell ignores.
